articles.title: 'It Was Really Great and Really Emotional' — Anthony Mackie Remembers Chris Evans Showing Him the Avengers: Endgame Script Early to Reveal How He'd Become Captain America
articles.summary: Anthony Mackie said Chris Evans told him how he'd become Captain America by showing him the Avengers: Endgame script early. The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) mainstay and former Falcon actor recalled finding out how Sam Wilson would take over the mantle as part of a conversation with Cigar…
body: "Chris Evans is somebody who I hold near and dear," he said. "We're at Chris' house, and because he's Captain America, he gets the [script] pages first. So he’s like, 'Yo, did you read the new scene?' I'm like, 'Nah, what's up?' So, he takes me down…and he gave me the script and let me read it.

"And it was really great and really emotional to learn it from a friend…I don’t know a lot of actors who would have appreciated or celebrated that moment with a fellow actor in that way because I was taking his job for all intents and purposes."

The end of Evans' time as Captain America marked the conclusion of an eight-year arc that saw his Steve Rogers appear in three standalone films, multiple team-up movies, a few fun cameos, and more. He quickly cemented himself as the most recognizable incarnation of the character and delivered fan-favorite stories that are still celebrated as some of the best the MCU has to offer today.

articles.title: 'Lanterns' Episode 7 Ending Explained: Antaan, Sinestro, and Who Killed Hal Jordan?
articles.summary: The penultimate episode of HBO’s Lanterns sees the core duo of John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) reunite in the strangest way imaginable. Now that we’re squarely in the present day, the mystery has shifted from the secret identity of Manhunter to who killed the real Hal…
body: Since this is the last episode before the finale, Lanterns delivers some pretty big moments, including a shocking cliffhanger at the end — and it also solves a mystery that didn’t really need to be solved at all.

Episode 6 revealed that Hal rented a storage unit in Rushville. Inside is a large alien vault similar to the one he used to store his lantern at his mansion. John and Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) aren’t able to open it since it requires that Hal identify himself aloud. A voicemail recording on Kerry’s phone can’t fool it, which is why John tricked Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion) into having Hal buried with his uniform and ring — all so John could dig up the body and retrieve the ring.

The Hal-ogram agrees to open the vault, but only if John lets him meet Kerry first. Inside the vault they find very little: a bag packed with supplies, including a handgun and a canteen, along with one of the black spheres we’ve seen throughout the season that can create portals. John describes the supplies as “stuff for a hike.” But considering the flashbacks we see during this episode, the idea of a “Jordan boy” having some kind of safe he leaves behind after his death takes on a whole new meaning.

articles.title: Avengers: Endgame Encore Collects $86 Million in Theaters as New Scenes Help MCU Fans Prep for Doomsday
articles.summary: Avengers: Endgame Encore dusted off an estimated $86 million at the box office as new scenes helped bring Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) fans back to theaters to prep for Doomsday.
body: It's a gargantuan opening weekend for Disney and Marvel's Infinity Saga-ending re-release that saw it rank atop global charts. Of its $86 million debut, it earned $26 million domestically and $60 million internationally.

For those unaware of why Avengers: Endgame is back in theaters, there are a few reasons audiences have shown up in droves to watch the seven-year-old MCU movie. First and foremost, the Encore re-release comes with a few minutes of extra footage that ties directly into this December's superhero crossover event film, Avengers: Doomsday. With director Joe Russo previously setting up the new clips as "critical" to the next movie's plot, it seemed inevitable that at least die-hard fans would show up.

articles.title: Philips Multigroom 7000 Series Is Nearly Half Price at Amazon UK Ahead of Prime Big Deal Days
articles.summary: Amazon UK is already dropping the price on a few grooming essentials ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, and this Philips Multigroom 7000 Series is currently £51.99, down from £94.99.
body: That's a pretty substantial £43 saving on an all-in-one trimmer designed to cover pretty much everything, from your beard and hair to your nose, ears and body. It comes with 17 attachments and 26 length settings ranging from 0.5mm to 20mm, so there's plenty of room to get the exact trim you're after without needing a drawer full of different gadgets.

The Multigroom 7000 uses self-sharpening full-metal steel blades, which Philips says stay as sharp as they were on day one without needing blade oil. There's also BeardSense technology, which scans beard density 125 times per second and automatically increases power when it detects thicker or longer hair.

For more precise work, the included precision comb offers 11 length settings between 1mm and 3mm in 0.2mm increments. There's also a narrow detail trimmer for sharper lines and finer work, alongside a metal trimmer for tidying up your cheeks, chin and neck.

At £51.99, it's a decent chunk below its usual £94.99 price, although it's worth remembering that Prime Big Deal Days itself doesn't officially start until October 6. Whether this particular deal sticks around until then, or gets replaced by an even lower price, remains to be seen.

articles.title: Netflix Tried to Bring Obsession Straight to Streaming Before It Exploded in Theaters
articles.summary: Director Curry Barker said Netflix bid to put Obsession straight to streaming before Focus Features helped it become the biggest box office success story of 2026. The comedian-turned-horror-filmmaker talked about the early days of his record-breaking low-budget flick during a conversation on Q with…
body: Barker said an early screening almost immediately resulted in "everybody" putting in offers to distribute Obsession. Neon, Focus, A24, and more wanted to bring Barker's twisted monkey's paw tale under their banner. Focus eventually won the war, but not before Netflix offered to throw a wrench into things.

"All of these companies are wanting to do your movie," Barker recalled hearing from his manager. "At this time, I'm still thinking maybe small theatrical release. Maybe they just want to acquire it, and also, as a director, I'm thinking, I'm scared of, 'Are they going to want to change my movie? Are they going to want to take out certain parts that I like?'
"So many questions were being thrown around. I think Netflix was in the conversation at one point. They put in an offer to just put it straight on Netflix. All of these conversations started."

articles.title: 9 Classic 'Far Side' Comics About Cats Being the Worst
articles.summary: In many of Gary Larson's Far Side comics, cats are depicted as the villains. Did he have something against cats?
body: Gary Larson loves cows. If you’re a reader of his comic strip The Far Side, it's clear that Larson adores the big, bovine creatures, as he often portrays them as adorable, if somewhat simple-minded heroes of his drawings. Even when they’re not good — like the strip where they’re plotting to eat a farmer — they’re portrayed in such a way that we want them to eat the farmer.

In contrast to the generally flattering light cows are portrayed in, Larson’s cats are always either villains or victims. They are the unruly, selfish pets of mankind, the ruthless enemies of dogs and rodents, or they're about to get a comeuppance that Larson appears to think they deserve. Perhaps, as a cat lover, I’m reading too much into this, but I’ve assembled these nine cartoons — one for each life of a cat — to present my case.

articles.summary: The Meg, starring Jason Statham, is an over-the-top action movie about a giant, thought-to-be-extinct shark causing all kinds of trouble
body: Jaws is the best shark movie ever made, and nothing will ever change that. Steven Spielberg's 1975 blockbuster is the perfect blend of action, suspense, and horror. It’s also one of the most important films in the history of cinema that forever changed the movie business. Because of that, it is literally impossible for some other shark movie to ever top it. Even making the attempt is a mistake. That is why all of the best shark movies out there try to do something different — like have Jason Statham face down a 75-foot prehistoric monster — which is the case in 2018’s immensely fun The Meg.

articles.title: Steam Week in Review: Great, haystack slop is a thing now
articles.summary: All the interesting Steam facts for the week ending September 27.
body: Clones have been a fixture in the games industry forever. For every Mario Bros there's a Giana Sisters, for every Stardew Valley there's a Fields of Mistria, and for every Needle In A Haystack Simulator there's a A Needle In a Haystack, or Needle in a Haystack, or Needle In A Haystack, or Needle In A Haystack - A Time For Goats, or Story of The Needle In a Haystack.

The total slopification of Steam continues apace and the recent spray of haystack games is the purest manifestation of this phenomenon. The first—as far as I can tell—was Needle In A Haystack Simulator, which is scheduled for release in Q4 2026. According to developers Studio Bitdot, a playtest in August attracted around 23,000 players, which is an astonishing figure for a game about finding a needle in a haystack.

articles.title: Xbox is reportedly paying a "fraction" of the $400 million Kojima quoted Sony for Physint
articles.summary: A reported $400 million budget for Hideo Kojima 's Physint has already been walked back over the weekend, with multiple outlets now saying Xbox is paying nowhere near that figure for Hideo Kojima's stealth game.
body: The number originated from Christopher Dring of The Game Business, who said on his podcast on Friday that Xbox was "signing Kojima for a project often referred to as Physint with a budget around $400 million".

Later, however, Dring himself clarified on X/Twitter that Xbox is likely paying "quite a bit less" than the figure Kojima had originally quoted Sony - Dring originally said he'd heard "everything from $300 million to $600 million, although it's $400 million that is the figure that is bandied around" - and Bloomberg's Jason Schreier said his own sources described Microsoft's negotiated figure as "significantly less than this".
Windows Central's Jez Corden went further, saying Xbox is paying only a "fraction" of it, although neither source reported an actual figure.

Physint, Kojima Productions' action-espionage title and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, was originally announced as a PlayStation project. Sony reportedly spent months negotiating with the studio before pulling its funding after the project exceeded budget and missed deadlines.

articles.title: After 12 years, Dark Souls 2 is finally playable in co-op without interruptions
articles.summary: I've always been content to admire the Dark Souls games from afar, rather than get particularly into them myself, and part of that is probably a crumb of leftover resentment from trying to wrangle the multiplayer features in those early games.
body: That's thanks to Yui, a soulslike modder who made similar mods for Elden Ring and Dark Souls. Her latest creation, Dark Souls 2: Seamless Co-op, just released into alpha last week and promises a straightforward co-op experience with up to five other players. "With this, it's theoretically possible to play the game from the tutorial up to the final boss completely in one co-op session," the release blog on Patreon notes. I'm sure one of you will be doing just that with a DDR mat or something.

While you could try to do a full playthrough with a buddy in the original Dark Souls 2, it'd involve a lot of stopping, starting, summoning, and fog walls. With this mod, there are no fog walls, progression is synced up, and the session won't end when someone dies—instead, they respawn at their last bonfire.

articles.title: Five Nights at Freddy's is coming to Fortnite for Fortnitemares
articles.summary: Epic has confirmed that Five Nights at Freddy's is joining Fortnite for this year's Fortnitemares event.
body: After months of rumours and teasing, a new trailer formally confirms that Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria will appear as a location on the map, with Freddy, Bonnie, Chica and Foxy all featuring as bosses that players can take on in a fight.
"It's almost showtime!" Epic announced. "The Fazbear Band has taken over Battle Royale. Face the animatronic animal bosses and survive the night… if you can. Fortnitemares begins 1st October!"

The crossover had been expected for a while, with the pizzeria itself appearing on the island during Fortnite's Override season, and recent Fortnitemares hinting at security cameras and FNAF dialogue.

Over the summer, Epic Games settled a court case against a contractor accused of leaking Fortnite information. Former contractor Hayden Cohen agreed to a judgment that bars them from "possessing, accessing, using, or disclosing any of Epic's confidential or trade secret information", including a ban on providing confidential information to other third parties, too.

articles.title: Minecraft is getting its first new dimension in 14 years, and it's called The Sift
articles.summary: Minecraft maker Mojang has announced The Sift, a new Minecraft dimension that will join the Overworld, the Nether, and The End when it launches on Java and Bedrock in 2027. It's the first new dimension added to the game since The End arrived in 2011.
body: The Sift will appear first in Minecraft Dungeons 2, slated for release on 29th September, before coming to the base game next year.

The Sift was announced during Minecraft Live on 26th September, alongside the wider Dungeons 2 reveal. We didn't get much information about it - Mojang is holding back most of the details for now - but did describe it as a new environment that will bring new biomes, mobs, and ways to play and explore. As yet, there's no firm release date.
"Minecraft Live revealed that the newest Minecraft dimension isn't just finding its home in Dungeons 2, it'll also be coming to Minecraft Java & Bedrock Edition next year," the team teased.

"This will be the first new dimension in over 14 years - joining the Overworld, the Nether and the End as our fourth dimension. During the broadcast, you got a glimpse into this dimension in Minecraft - and even one of the mobs that calls it home. But surely that's not enough! Luckily you can experience it for yourself in Minecraft Dungeons 2 - coming September 29, 2026."
